Quick update from our side about the 429 spike you saw this morning. We observed a sudden burst of token rejections routed to your tenant (tenant_id: starnova-prod) between 07:42–07:55 PDT — this manifested as short-lived 429 responses for a subset of requests.

What we did immediately:
- Applied an emergency override to your tenant’s rate-cap mapping to prevent further rejections (no code changes on your side).
- Scoped a conservative temporary increase to the per-tenant token allowance for traffic coming from your primary API key.
- Opened an incident and assigned it to our inference routing team.

Attachments: ratecap-config-diff.txt (diff of the override we applied), remediation-playbook.pdf

Next steps we’re executing now (ETA in this email):
1) Engineering will validate the root cause and confirm a permanent fix (by EOD tomorrow).
2) We’ll schedule a short maintenance window if a live change is required (we’ll coordinate timing with your ops team).
3) We will provide a short post-incident summary with timeline, cause, actions, and a proposal for a small service credit for the affected window.

Can you confirm whether you saw downstream request retries that resulted in duplicate records on your side? If so, tell us which endpoints were affected (trace IDs help).

Sorry for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority. I’ll keep you posted as we learn more.

Thanks,

Ben / team — quick technical findings from the routing side:

Summary:
- Root cause: a recent config merge (internal change INF-RATE-MAP #2314) introduced an unexpected precedence change between global rate caps and tenant-specific profiles. For tenants with a custom mapping (StarNova), an older rate profile was incorrectly picked up during a fast path evaluation which temporarily lowered the token allowance and produced 429 responses.
- Scope: affected ~0.4% of requests to the tenant’s prod key; spike window we’ve confirmed is 2026-07-19T07:42:00Z–2026-07-19T07:55:00Z (UTC).
- Why duplicates happened: client-side retries retried idempotent ingest calls; because the server returned 429 before accepting the request, retries were re-sent and some later retries succeeded, producing duplicate ingests.

Immediate remediation applied (yesterday): emergency override to tenant mapping (kept live), re-prioritized rate profile selection so tenant profile always wins when present.

Planned permanent fix:
1) Back out the precedence regression in INF-RATE-MAP #2314 and add a unit test to protect mapping precedence — deploy to canary tonight (22:00 PDT).
2) Run a controlled rollout to prod across 3 waves (canary -> 50% -> 100%) with health checks and a rollback flag (total ~45 minutes).
3) Post-deploy audit to validate token accounting for the affected window.

Estimated exposure & proposed credit:
- Token exposure (approx): 1.9M tokens between 07:42–08:05 PDT (this is an upper bound).
- Suggested one-time credit: $380 (calculated using your current token rate and a conservative 20% allowance for retries and successful tokens). We can adjust if StarNova’s billing rules differ.

Attachments: ratecap-config-diff.txt (the emergency override), remediation-playbook.pdf (change plan + testing checklist).

Schedule request: canary deploy at 22:00 PDT tonight (2026-07-20). Elena indicated they are available after 22:00 for coordination.

Karthik
Sr. Product Engineer, Inference Routing

Subject: Resolution & post-incident summary (StarNova) — action items and credit

Hi Elena —

Thanks for your patience while our team completed the remediation and validation. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps.

Incident window (confirmed): 2026-07-19T07:42:00Z–2026-07-19T07:55:00Z (UTC) — corresponds to 00:42–00:55 UTC on our telemetry / 07:42–07:55 PDT local.
Root cause: a precedence regression in a rate-cap config merge caused tenant-specific profiles to be bypassed under a fast-path optimization.
Actions taken:
- Emergency override applied (immediate mitigation) — 2026-07-19T08:00 PDT.
- Precedence fix deployed to canary and rolled to prod in three waves on 2026-07-20 22:00–22:45 PDT with health checks and rollback gate.
- Post-deploy audit completed; audit validated token accounting and confirmed no further 429s for your tenant after the fix.

Customer impact:
- Affected ~0.4% of requests during the window; we estimate up to 1.9M tokens potentially involved (upper bound).

Credit proposal: $380 one-time credit applied to your July invoice to cover potential retry/duplicate exposure. If you prefer we can open a detailed billing review with finance; let me know.

Follow-ups and recommended actions:
1) We recommend you run a short de-duplication job for ingest events with timestamps between 2026-07-19T07:45–08:05 PDT (we’ll share trace IDs on request).
2) We’ll add an integration test to your onboarding guidance that detects unexpected 429 patterns during low-volume canaries.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-minute readout next week with your ops and our routing team to walk through the fix and the test coverage. Proposed times: Tue 2026-07-27 09:00 PDT or Wed 2026-07-28 16:00 PDT — which works best?

Attachments: remediation-playbook.pdf, ratecap-config-diff.txt
Related ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 (postmortem doc will be added here).

Again, sorry for the disruption. If you want the billing review escalated to finance, I can loop in our billing lead.
